pendingSellers.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation. SELECT COUNT(*) FROM shopping_mall_sellers WHERE approvalStatus = 'pending'. Counts sellers awaiting administrator approval.

approvedSellers.description: Number of seller accounts that have been approved and are currently active (not suspended or banned).
approvedSellers.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation. SELECT COUNT(*) FROM shopping_mall_sellers WHERE approvalStatus = 'approved' AND isSuspended = false AND isBanned = false. Counts active approved sellers.

suspendedSellers.description: Number of seller accounts that have been temporarily suspended by administrators for policy violations.
suspendedSellers.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation. SELECT COUNT(*) FROM shopping_mall_sellers WHERE isSuspended = true AND isBanned = false. Counts sellers temporarily suspended by administrators.

rejectedSellers.description: Number of seller applications that were rejected by administrators during the approval process.
rejectedSellers.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation. SELECT COUNT(*) FROM shopping_mall_sellers WHERE approvalStatus = 'rejected'. Counts seller applications that were rejected by administrators.

bannedSellers.description: Number of seller accounts that have been permanently banned from the platform due to severe policy violations.
bannedSellers.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation. SELECT COUNT(*) FROM shopping_mall_sellers WHERE isBanned = true. Counts sellers permanently banned from the platform.

totalProducts.description: Total number of active product listings on the platform, excluding deleted products.
totalProducts.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation. SELECT COUNT(*) FROM shopping_mall_products WHERE isDeleted = false. Counts all non-deleted products across all sellers.

activeProducts.description: Number of products that have at least one variant currently in stock and available for purchase.
activeProducts.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation. SELECT COUNT(*) FROM shopping_mall_products WHERE isDeleted = false AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM shopping_mall_product_variants WHERE productId = shopping_mall_products.id AND isDeleted = false AND stockQuantity > 0). Counts products with at least one variant in stock.

inactiveProducts.description: Number of products that exist but have no variants currently available in stock (all variants are out of stock or deleted).
inactiveProducts.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation. SELECT COUNT(*) FROM shopping_mall_products WHERE isDeleted = false AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM shopping_mall_product_variants WHERE productId = shopping_mall_products.id AND isDeleted = false AND stockQuantity > 0). Counts products with no variants in stock or all variants deleted.

outOfStockVariants.description: Total number of product variants (SKUs) that are currently out of stock, regardless of product status.
outOfStockVariants.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation. SELECT COUNT(*) FROM shopping_mall_product_variants WHERE isDeleted = false AND stockQuantity = 0. Counts all product variants (SKUs) that are currently out of stock.

productsWithZeroVariants.description: Number of product listings that have no variants defined (zero SKUs), making them non-purchasable.
productsWithZeroVariants.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation. SELECT COUNT(*) FROM shopping_mall_products WHERE isDeleted = false AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM shopping_mall_product_variants WHERE productId = shopping_mall_products.id AND isDeleted = false). Counts products with no variants defined at all.

totalOrders.description: Total number of orders placed on the platform since its inception.
totalOrders.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation. SELECT COUNT(*) FROM shopping_mall_orders. Counts all orders created on the platform regardless of status.

paidOrders.description: Number of orders that have been successfully paid for by customers.
paidOrders.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation. SELECT COUNT(*) FROM shopping_mall_orders WHERE paymentStatus = 'paid'. Counts orders where payment has been successfully processed.

shippedOrders.description: Number of orders that have been packed and shipped by sellers (at least one shipment has been created).
shippedOrders.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation. SELECT COUNT(*) FROM shopping_mall_orders WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM shopping_mall_shipments WHERE shopping_mall_shipments.orderId = shopping_mall_orders.id). Counts orders with at least one shipment created.

deliveredOrders.description: Number of orders where all items have been marked as delivered by customers.
deliveredOrders.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation. SELECT COUNT(*) FROM shopping_mall_orders WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM shopping_mall_shipments WHERE shopping_mall_shipments.orderId = shopping_mall_orders.id AND is_delivered = true). Counts orders with all shipments marked as delivered.

cancelledOrders.description: Number of orders that have been fully cancelled and are no longer active.
cancelledOrders.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation. SELECT COUNT(*) FROM shopping_mall_orders WHERE status = 'cancelled'. Counts orders that have been fully cancelled by customers or administrators.

refundedOrders.description: Number of orders that have been approved for refund, either partially or fully.
refundedOrders.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation. SELECT COUNT(*) FROM shopping_mall_orders WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM shopping_mall_refund_requests WHERE shopping_mall_refund_requests.orderId = shopping_mall_orders.id AND status = 'approved'). Counts orders with at least one approved refund request.

totalCustomers.description: Total number of customer accounts registered on the platform, excluding banned accounts.
totalCustomers.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation. SELECT COUNT(*) FROM shopping_mall_customers WHERE isBanned = false. Counts all non-banned customer accounts registered on the platform.

pendingCancellations.description: Number of cancellation requests submitted by customers that are still pending approval from sellers or administrators.
pendingCancellations.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation. SELECT COUNT(*) FROM shopping_mall_cancellation_requests WHERE status = 'pending'. Counts cancellation requests awaiting seller or administrator response.

pendingRefunds.description: Number of refund requests submitted by customers that are still pending approval from sellers or administrators.
pendingRefunds.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation. SELECT COUNT(*) FROM shopping_mall_refund_requests WHERE status = 'pending'. Counts refund requests awaiting seller or administrator response.

activeSessions.description: Total number of active user sessions (customer, seller, admin, super admin) with valid, unexpired JWT tokens.
activeSessions.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation. SELECT COUNT(*) FROM shopping_mall_customer_sessions WHERE expiresAt > NOW() UNION ALL SELECT COUNT(*) FROM shopping_mall_admin_sessions WHERE expiresAt > NOW() UNION ALL SELECT COUNT(*) FROM shopping_mall_seller_sessions WHERE expiresAt > NOW() UNION ALL SELECT COUNT(*) FROM shopping_mall_super_admin_sessions WHERE expiresAt > NOW(). Counts all active JWT sessions across all actor types.

systemUptimeHours.description: Continuous uptime of the platform system since the last restart, measured in full hours. Indicates system stability and reliability.
systemUptimeHours.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation. Based on monitoring system. Retains the timestamp of last system restart and calculates difference from current time in hours. Must be maintained by system monitoring service.

averageOrderValue.description: Average monetary value of completed and paid orders on the platform. Indicates overall customer spending patterns.
averageOrderValue.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation. SELECT AVG(totalPrice) FROM shopping_mall_orders WHERE paymentStatus = 'paid' AND totalPrice > 0. Calculates mean order value for all paid orders. Uses real-time calculation to avoid stale data.

sellerApprovalRate.description: Percentage of seller applications that have been approved out of all non-banned seller applications received. Measures platform openness to new sellers.
sellerApprovalRate.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation. SELECT CAST(COUNT(CASE WHEN approvalStatus = 'approved' THEN 1 END) AS FLOAT) / COUNT(*) FROM shopping_mall_sellers WHERE isBanned = false AND approvalStatus IN ('approved', 'pending', 'rejected'). Calculates percentage of approved applications among total non-banned seller applications.

customerRetentionRate.description: Percentage of customers who have placed more than one order within the last 90 days, indicating user retention and platform loyalty.
customerRetentionRate.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation. SELECT CAST(COUNT(DISTINCT customerId) AS FLOAT) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM shopping_mall_customers WHERE isBanned = false) FROM shopping_mall_orders WHERE createdAt >= DATE_SUB(NOW(), INTERVAL 90 DAY). Counts customers who placed two or more orders in the last 90 days as returning customers.

email.description: The email address of the authenticated administrator, used for identity verification and communication purposes.

id.x-autobe-specification: Mapped from JWT subject claim (admin_id) in authentication token. No direct database column mapping as this is an authentication response DTO.

token.x-autobe-specification: Constructs the full authentication token structure by combining access and refresh tokens retrieved from shopping_mall_admin_sessions table. These tokens are stored with expiration metadata and used for token refresh operations.

totalRevenue.description: Total revenue generated from all completed sales transactions on the platform, calculated as the sum of total_amount fields for sales with status 'completed'.

transactionCount.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation: COUNT(*) FROM shopping_mall_sales WHERE status = 'completed'. Represents the total number of completed sales transactions.

averageTransactionValue.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation: AVG(total_amount) FROM shopping_mall_sales WHERE status = 'completed'. Represents the arithmetic mean of all completed sales transaction amounts.

totalUnitsSold.description: Total quantity of products sold across all completed sales transactions on the platform, calculated by summing the quantity_sold field for all sales with status 'completed'.
totalUnitsSold.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation: SUM(quantity_sold) FROM shopping_mall_sales WHERE status = 'completed'. Represents the total quantity of products sold across all completed transactions.

IShoppingMallSaleViewStat.description: Comprehensive sales performance metrics summarizing total revenue, transaction count, average transaction value, and total units sold. This object provides high-level analytics derived from completed sales in the shopping_mall_sales table, enabling business intelligence and dashboard reporting without exposing individual transaction data. The values are computed in real-time using SQL aggregation functions and are cached for performance.

Filtered for completed sales only. Results cached for 5 minutes. All values are calculated dynamically from database, no direct table mapping. Values are always non-negative numbers.

total_product_count.description: Total number of active (non-deleted) products listed across all sellers on the platform.
total_product_count.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation. SELECT COUNT(*) FROM shopping_mall_products WHERE seller_id IN (SELECT id FROM shopping_mall_sellers) AND is_deleted = false. Counts all products created by all sellers that are not marked as deleted.

total_order_item_count.description: Total number of paid order items across all orders on the platform, excluding cancelled or refunded items.
total_order_item_count.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation. SELECT COUNT(*) FROM shopping_mall_order_items WHERE order_id IN (SELECT id FROM shopping_mall_orders) AND cancel_request_id IS NULL AND refund_request_id IS NULL. Counts all order items that have been successfully paid and not cancelled or refunded.

pending_cancellation_count.description: Total number of cancellation requests across all order items that are currently pending approval from sellers or administrators.
pending_cancellation_count.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation. SELECT COUNT(*) FROM shopping_mall_cancellation_requests WHERE status = 'pending' AND order_item_id IN (SELECT id FROM shopping_mall_order_items). Counts all cancellation requests that are still pending approval or rejection by a seller or admin.

pending_refund_count.description: Total number of refund requests across all order items that are currently pending approval from sellers or administrators.
pending_refund_count.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation. SELECT COUNT(*) FROM shopping_mall_refund_requests WHERE status = 'pending' AND order_item_id IN (SELECT id FROM shopping_mall_order_items). Counts all refund requests that are still pending approval or rejection by a seller or admin.

IShoppingMallAdminSellerDashboard.description: Summary of seller platform performance metrics for an administrative dashboard view. All values are non-negative integers representing numeric counts from system-wide aggregations.

All metrics are raw counts calculated from non-deleted records, grouped across all sellers. It does not represent a physical database table but a computed view used for administrative dashboard metrics.

status.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_admin_requests.status field. Enum value representing the current state of the administrator request (pending/approved/rejected).

respondedBy.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_admin_requests.responded_by column. UUID of the super administrator who processed this administrator application request.

revenue.description: Total revenue generated by this promotional campaign in the platform's base currency (USD).

IShoppingMallAdminPasswordReset.x-autobe-specification: This DTO represents an administrator application request record stored in the shopping_mall_admin_requests table. It is a transient tracking entity generated when a customer or seller submits an admin application. The record is created by client code using adminRequestId, requestedAt, and userId from the authenticated session, with status pre-set to 'pending' and reason from the request body. External system services update status to 'approved' or 'rejected' after super-admin review. This model does not represent a core business entity with direct CRUD operations but serves as an immutable audit trail for access control decisions. All fields are required and immutable after creation.

total_sales.description: Total number of sales transactions completed by the seller's shop.
total_sales.x-autobe-specification: Derived metric from shopping_mall_sale_view_stats: COUNT DISTINCT shopping_mall_sale_id for the authenticated seller's account. Represents unique sales transactions.

revenue.description: Total revenue generated from completed sales, excluding refunds and cancellations.
revenue.x-autobe-specification: Derived metric from shopping_mall_sale_view_stats: SUM of sale values (price * quantity) for the authenticated seller's account, excluding cancellations and refunds. The sale field contains the monetary value of each sale.

total_orders.description: Total number of unique orders completed by customers purchasing from this seller's shop.
total_orders.x-autobe-specification: Derived metric from shopping_mall_sale_view_stats: COUNT DISTINCT order_id derived from shopping_mall_sale_id (mapped to orders) for the authenticated seller's account. Represents unique completed orders.

customer_count.description: Total number of unique customers who have made at least one purchase from this seller's shop.
customer_count.x-autobe-specification: Derived metric from shopping_mall_sale_view_stats: COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) derived from the relationship between shopping_mall_sale_id and customer sessions or orders for the authenticated seller's account. Represents unique customers who made purchases.

total_units_sold.description: Total number of product units sold across all completed orders in the seller's shop.
total_units_sold.x-autobe-specification: Derived metric from shopping_mall_sale_view_stats: SUM of unit quantities extracted from sale details for the authenticated seller's account, representing total items sold across all orders.

average_order_value.description: Average amount spent per completed order, calculated as total revenue divided by total number of orders.
average_order_value.x-autobe-specification: Derived metric from shopping_mall_sale_view_stats: revenue / total_orders. Uses pre-aggregated values from shopping_mall_sale_view_stats to compute average order value across all completed orders, where revenue is SUM(sale) and total_orders is COUNT(DISTINCT order_id).

customer_retention_rate.description: Percentage of customers who have made more than one purchase from this seller's shop, indicating customer loyalty.
customer_retention_rate.x-autobe-specification: Derived metric from shopping_mall_sale_view_stats: (customers with multiple orders / customer_count) * 100. Calculated by identifying customers with multiple shopping_mall_sale_id entries (mapped to customer_id) and dividing by total unique customer_count.

IShoppingMallSaleSnapshot.description:
Contains aggregated performance summary metrics for the seller's shop on the shoppingMall platform.

This summary provides key business indicators for a seller's shop performance including total sales volume, revenue generated, number of orders processed, average order value, unique customer count, customer retention rate (percentage of customers who made multiple purchases), and total units sold across all products in the seller's shop.

All metrics are computed from immutable order snapshots that preserve the exact state of products, variants, seller profiles, and pricing at the moment of purchase, ensuring historical accuracy. The calculation excludes any products or variants that have been deleted by the seller after the order was placed.

The revenue figure includes only completed payments and excludes refunds or cancellations. The average order value and number of customers represent unique customers who completed any purchase from the seller's shop. Customer retention is calculated based on repeat purchase behavior, defined as customers making more than one purchase.

This information is used by sellers to understand their shop's performance, identify trends, and make informed business decisions.
IShoppingMallSaleSnapshot.x-autobe-specification: Source: Aggregates data from shopping_mall_sale_view_stats table for the authenticated seller. Computes all metrics using the available columns: id, shopping_mall_sale_id, and sale. The aggregation logic must be implemented through server-side computations using the schema's available fields, with seller_id from authentication context. All calculations exclude deleted products/variants. Since the schema does not expose direct columns for sales_count, total_revenue, order_count, unique_customer_count, or unit_quantity, these are computed metrics aggregated from available data.

status.description: The status of the administrative action, which is always 'rejected' for this response type.
status.x-autobe-specification: Fixed constant value 'rejected' indicating the seller application has been formally denied by an administrator. This value is set programmatically and never changes.

timestamp.description: The precise timestamp when the seller application was rejected, in ISO 8601 format (UTC).
timestamp.x-autobe-specification: Server-generated ISO 8601 timestamp (UTC) capturing the exact time when the rejection action was processed by the system. This is not a database field but a system-generated audit time.

IShoppingMallDeliveryConfirmation.description: Confirmation message returned after an administrator successfully rejects a seller application. Contains the fixed status 'rejected' and server-generated timestamp to acknowledge the administrative action has been processed.
IShoppingMallDeliveryConfirmation.x-autobe-specification: Response DTO for admin rejection of seller application. Returns fixed status 'rejected' and server-generated timestamp. This is a simple acknowledgment type that does not map to any database table, but is constructed in-memory upon successful completion of the rejection operation.

totalSales.description: Total sales amount generated from all completed orders in the current month.
totalSales.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation. SUM of order totals from shopping_mall_orders table for current month.

averageOrderValue.description: Average value of all completed orders in the current month.
averageOrderValue.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation. AVG of order totals from shopping_mall_orders table for current month.

inventoryTurnoverRate.description: The number of times inventory is sold and replaced over a monthly period. Measures inventory efficiency and turnover speed.
inventoryTurnoverRate.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation. Calculated as (total cost of goods sold / average inventory value). COGS sourced from shopping_mall_orders based on product variant prices, average inventory value from shopping_mall_inventory_records. Time period is current month.

conversionRate.description: The percentage of product views that result in completed purchases. Measures effectiveness of product presentation and customer intent.
conversionRate.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation. Division: number of completed purchases (from shopping_mall_orders) divided by total product views (from shopping_mall_sale_view_stats). Ratio expressed as decimal (0 to 1).

customerRetentionRate.description: The percentage of customers who made more than one purchase within the current reporting period. Measures customer loyalty and platform stickiness.
customerRetentionRate.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation. Percentage of customers who made repeat purchases within the current month. Calculated as: (unique customers with >1 order) / (total unique customers who made purchases) * 100.

topProducts.description: The 10 best-performing products in terms of total sales volume during the current month. Each entry contains product information and total sales count.
topProducts.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation. Top 10 products by total sales volume (quantity * unit price) across shopping_mall_orders and shopping_mall_order_items tables. Each item includes productId and total sales count.

bottomProducts.description: The 10 worst-performing products in terms of total sales volume during the current month. Each entry contains product information and total sales count.
bottomProducts.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation. Bottom 10 products by total sales volume (quantity * unit price) across shopping_mall_orders and shopping_mall_order_items tables. Each item includes productId and total sales count.

IShoppingMallSale.description: Comprehensive sales performance metrics for the shoppingMall platform. Contains key business KPIs for admin decision-making, including total sales, average order value, inventory turnover rate, conversion rate from product views to purchases, customer retention rate, and lists of top and bottom performing products.
IShoppingMallSale.x-autobe-specification: This is a computed/aggregated response type for sales performance metrics. Data sourced from: totalSales from SUM of order values in shopping_mall_orders; averageOrderValue from AVG of order totals; inventoryTurnoverRate from (total cost of goods sold / average inventory value), where cost of goods sold is from shopping_mall_orders and inventory value is from shopping_mall_inventory_records; conversionRate from (number of completed purchases / number of product views) using shopping_mall_sale_view_stats; customerRetentionRate from percentage of customers who made repeat purchases within the time period; topProducts from top 10 products by sales volume across shopping_mall_orders and shopping_mall_order_items; bottomProducts from bottom 10 products by sales volume across the same tables. Calculations use time period of current month. All values are zero or positive. When no data, numeric values should be 0. topProducts and bottomProducts should be arrays of objects with at least productId and salesCount.

imageId.description: Unique identifier of the product image to be reordered in the gallery sequence.
imageId.x-autobe-specification: References image_id from shopping_mall_product_images table via foreign key relationship. Value used for lookup and validation against existing product images in the system.

imageOrder.description: The desired zero-indexed display order position for this product image in the gallery.
imageOrder.x-autobe-specification: The desired zero-indexed display position for this product image in the gallery of a product. This value is applied as a direct update to the image_order column in the shopping_mall_product_images table to reorder image sequence.

IShoppingMallProductImage.IReorderItem.description: An individual instruction to reorder a specific product image by its unique identifier to a new position in the sequence. Represents one item in the image ordering array of the reorder operation.
IShoppingMallProductImage.IReorderItem.x-autobe-specification: Transient request DTO used exclusively in PUT /products/{productId}/images/reorder endpoint to specify reordering instructions for product images. This is not a persistent entity - represents a client-side instruction for changing image display order. The entire array is sent as JSON body and processed as atomic operation with no individual persistence.

status.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation: Derived from order_items status. If all order_items are 'delivered': 'delivered'; if any order_items are 'refunded': 'refunded'; if any order_items are 'cancelled': 'cancelled'; if all order_items are 'paid' and at least one is 'shipped': 'shipped'; if all order_items are 'paid' and none shipped: 'paid'; if any order_items are 'shipped' and some 'delivered' and some not: 'partially_completed'.
status.description: Current lifecycle status of the order: 'paid' (completed payment), 'shipped' (items dispatched), 'delivered' (fulfilled and received), 'cancelled' (request processed), 'refunded' (payment returned), or 'partially_completed' (some items delivered but others still pending). Can be null if status is not yet determined.

id.description: Unique identifier for the order in the system, represented as a UUID.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_orders.id column. UUID primary key for order identification.

orderNumber.description: Unique alphanumeric order number in format 'ORD-YYYYMMDD-NNNN' for customer reference and transaction tracking.
orderNumber.x-autobe-specification: Computed field: Concatenates 'ORD-' prefix with the 8-digit formatted creation date from shopping_mall_orders.created_at and a zero-padded 4-digit sequence number derived from the order's id hash. Format: 'ORD-YYYYMMDD-NNNN'.

totalPrice.description: Total monetary value of the entire order in the base currency at the time of purchase, including items, taxes, and discounts.
totalPrice.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation: SUM of (order_items.price * order_items.quantity) from all order_items associated with this order, where order_items.order_id = shopping_mall_orders.id. Includes taxes and discounts applied to each order item.

IShoppingMallOrder.ISummary.description: Lightweight summary representation of an order for display in list views such as customer order history. Contains essential information for browsing: unique identifier, order number, total price, current status, and creation timestamp. Excludes detailed order items, shipping addresses, and shipment information for optimal performance in list contexts.
IShoppingMallOrder.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Summary DTO for shopping_mall_orders table. This DTO provides a lightweight representation of an order for list displays, excluding detailed items and shipping information for performance optimization in UI contexts. The orderNumber, totalPrice, status, and createdAt fields are computed: orderNumber is formatted from order ID and creation time, totalPrice is aggregated from order_items, status is derived from order_items item statuses, and createdAt is read directly from the database. Only 'id' is a direct mapping from the database.

access.description:
Short-lived JWT access token for authenticating API requests.

This token must be included in the Authorization header using the Bearer
scheme (e.g., `Authorization: Bearer {access}`) for all endpoints requiring
authentication. The token contains encoded claims including user identity,
roles, and permissions. Typically expires within 15-60 minutes for
security; use the refresh token to obtain a new access token when expired.
access.x-autobe-specification: JWT access token. Use in Authorization header as "Bearer {access}".

refresh.description:
Long-lived refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.

Used to request new access tokens when the current access token expires,
allowing session continuation without re-authentication. Should be stored
securely and transmitted only to the token refresh endpoint. Typical
lifetime ranges from 7 to 30 days depending on security requirements.
refresh.x-autobe-specification: Refresh token for obtaining new access tokens without re-authentication.

expired_at.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp when the access token expires.

After this timestamp, the access token will be rejected by authenticated
endpoints. Clients should proactively refresh before expiration to maintain
seamless user experience. A common strategy is to refresh when remaining
time falls below 5 minutes. This timestamp is also embedded within the JWT
itself as the "exp" claim.
expired_at.x-autobe-specification: Access token expiration timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

refreshable_until.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp indicating the absolute session expiration deadline.

Represents the latest possible time the refresh token can be used. Once
this timestamp is reached, the user must fully re-authenticate with
credentials. This defines the maximum session duration regardless of
activity. If refresh token rotation is enabled, this deadline may extend
with each successful refresh.
refreshable_until.x-autobe-specification: Refresh token expiration timestamp. Re-authentication required after this time.

IShoppingMallAuthorizationToken.description:
JWT-based authorization token pair with expiration metadata.

Provides a complete authentication token structure containing both access and
refresh tokens along with their respective expiration timestamps. This
dual-token pattern enables secure, stateless authentication with automatic
session renewal capabilities.

The access token is short-lived for security, while the refresh token allows
obtaining new access tokens without requiring the user to re-enter
credentials. This structure is automatically included in authentication
responses across all generated backend applications.
IShoppingMallAuthorizationToken.x-autobe-specification: Dual-token authentication structure with access/refresh tokens and expiration info.

recipientName.description: Full name of the person who will receive the package. This is captured verbatim at order time to ensure delivery accuracy.
recipientName.x-autobe-specification: This property is part of the embedded JSON object stored in shopping_mall_orders.shippingAddress. The value comes from the 'recipientName' key within the JSON structure.

streetAddress.description: Complete physical delivery address including number, street name, building, and apartment/unit information. Must be sufficient for a courier to locate the delivery point.
streetAddress.x-autobe-specification: This property is part of the embedded JSON object stored in shopping_mall_orders.shippingAddress. The value comes from the 'streetAddress' key within the JSON structure.

city.description: City or municipality name where the delivery address is located. Used for sorting, shipping zone determination, and local delivery routing.
city.x-autobe-specification: This property is part of the embedded JSON object stored in shopping_mall_orders.shippingAddress. The value comes from the 'city' key within the JSON structure.

stateProvince.description: State or province where the delivery address is located. Used for tax calculation, shipping fee determination, and regional regulations. Optional but recommended for accurate fulfillment.
stateProvince.x-autobe-specification: This property is part of the embedded JSON object stored in shopping_mall_orders.shippingAddress. The value comes from the 'stateProvince' key within the JSON structure.

postalCode.description: Postal or ZIP code of the delivery address. Critical for accurate shipping carrier routing and delivery time estimation.
postalCode.x-autobe-specification: This property is part of the embedded JSON object stored in shopping_mall_orders.shippingAddress. The value comes from the 'postalCode' key within the JSON structure.

country.description: Country of the delivery address, specified as a two-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code. Required for international shipping compliance, taxes, and customs processing.
country.x-autobe-specification: This property is part of the embedded JSON object stored in shopping_mall_orders.shippingAddress. The value comes from the 'country' key within the JSON structure.

phoneNumber.description: Contact phone number for delivery personnel to reach the recipient if needed. Optional and stored exactly as provided by the customer at time of order.
phoneNumber.x-autobe-specification: This property is part of the embedded JSON object stored in shopping_mall_orders.shippingAddress. The value comes from the 'phoneNumber' key within the JSON structure.

isDefault.description: Indicates if this address was the customer's default address at the time the order was placed. Preserved for historical context and user interface display only. Does not influence system logic, as this address is already captured as a snapshot.
isDefault.x-autobe-specification: This property is part of the embedded JSON object stored in shopping_mall_orders.shippingAddress. The value comes from the 'isDefault' key within the JSON structure.

IShoppingMallCustomerAddress.description: Immutable shipping address snapshot captured at time of order placement. Contains all mandatory components for delivery: recipient name, complete street address, city, postal code, and country. Optional fields include state/province for tax/shipping calculations and phone number for delivery notifications. The isDefault flag indicates whether this was the customer's default address at the time of order creation, preserved for historical context only.
IShoppingMallCustomerAddress.x-autobe-specification: Embedded JSON structure stored directly in the shopping_mall_orders.shippingAddress column. This immutable snapshot captures the complete customer shipping address state (recipientName, streetAddress, city, stateProvince, postalCode, country, phoneNumber, isDefault) at the moment of order placement. All address components are stored as a single JSON object to preserve historical integrity and prevent changes to customer profiles from altering past order records. The entire object is stored verbatim from the customer's checkout submission without normalization or component-level separation in the database.

message.description: Confirmation message indicating the email verification token has been successfully resent to the super administrator's registered email address. The system has initiated the background process to deliver a new verification email with a fresh token.
message.x-autobe-specification: Contains standardized success message text 'Verification email resent successfully' that confirms the backend has accepted and queued the email resend request. This is a static, pre-defined message presented to API clients as confirmation that the operation was accepted for processing. Message text is not derived from database or other data sources - it is a hardcoded response string generated by the service layer.

IShoppingMallSuperAdminEmailVerification.description: Confirmation response indicating the email verification token has been successfully resent to the super administrator's registered email address. The system has initiated the background process to deliver a new verification email with a fresh token.
IShoppingMallSuperAdminEmailVerification.x-autobe-specification: Pure response type for email verification resend operations. This schema represents a success confirmation message returned by the system after triggering the email resend process. No database persistence occurs during this operation. The 'message' field contains a standardized success message text that confirms the email verification token has been successfully queued for resending to the super administrator's registered email address. This is a stateless response type used exclusively for API client feedback. All state management and email sending occur asynchronously in the backend service layer.

imageId.description: Unique identifier of the product image to be reordered in the gallery sequence.
imageId.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_product_images.id column. Used as primary key to identify image for reordering operations.

IShoppingMallProductImage.ISummary.description: A lightweight summary of a product image containing only the unique identifier needed for reordering operations in the product gallery.
IShoppingMallProductImage.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Summary DTO representation of a product image for reordering operations. This DTO contains only the minimal required fields for an image reordering API endpoint. It maps directly to the shopping_mall_product_images table.

instruction:
### E2E Test Instructions

#### **Authentication API Tests**

##### **POST /v1/auth/register**
- Test valid customer registration with unique email → expect 201
- Test valid seller registration with unique email → expect 201
- Test registration with duplicate email → expect 409
- Test registration with invalid email format → expect 400
- Test registration with password < 8 chars → expect 400
- Test registration without role → expect 400
- Test registration with invalid role → expect 400

##### **POST /v1/auth/login**
- Test login with valid credentials → expect 200 and JWT token
- Test login with invalid email → expect 401
- Test login with invalid password → expect 401
- Test login with banned account → expect 403
- Test login with inactive account → expect 403

##### **PUT /v1/auth/password**
- Test password change with correct current password → expect 200
- Test password change with incorrect current password → expect 400
- Test password change with new password < 8 chars → expect 400
- Test password change without authentication → expect 401
- Test password change with same current password → expect 400 (or 200? clarify business rule)

##### **DELETE /v1/auth/account**
- Test customer account deletion → expect 204
- Test seller account deletion with no pending orders → expect 204
- Test seller account deletion with pending paid order → expect 400
- Test seller account deletion with pending cancellation request → expect 400
- Test account deletion without authentication → expect 401


#### **Customer Profile API Tests**

##### **GET /v1/customers/me**
- Test authenticated customer profile retrieval → expect 200 with correct profile
- Test profile retrieval without authentication → expect 401
- Test profile retrieval as seller → expect 403

##### **PUT /v1/customers/me**
- Test update display name → expect 200 with updated name
- Test update phone number → expect 200 with updated number
- Test update both fields → expect 200 with both updated
- Test update profile without authentication → expect 401
- Test update profile as seller → expect 403


#### **Address Management API Tests**

##### **GET /v1/addresses**
- Test list all addresses for authenticated customer → expect 200 with correct array
- Test address list with no addresses → expect 200 with empty array
- Test address list without authentication → expect 401

##### **POST /v1/addresses**
- Test create new address with all required fields → expect 201
- Test create address with isDefault=true → verify other addresses become non-default
- Test create address without required fields → expect 400
- Test create address as non-customer → expect 403

##### **PUT /v1/addresses/{addressId}**
- Test update address fields → expect 200 with updated values
- Test update address to default → verify other addresses become non-default
- Test update address not owned by user → expect 403
- Test update address without authentication → expect 401

##### **DELETE /v1/addresses/{addressId}**
- Test delete address → expect 204
- Test delete default address when other addresses exist → expect 204
- Test delete last address → expect 400 (must leave at least one)
- Test delete address not owned by user → expect 403
- Test delete non-existent address → expect 404

##### **GET /v1/addresses/default**
- Test get default address when set → expect 200 with correct default
- Test get default address when none set → expect 404
- Test get default address without authentication → expect 401


#### **Seller Account API Tests**

##### **GET /v1/sellers/me**
- Test authenticated seller profile retrieval → expect 200 with correct profile
- Test profile retrieval without authentication → expect 401
- Test profile retrieval as customer → expect 403

##### **PUT /v1/sellers/me**
- Test update shop name → expect 200
- Test update shop description → expect 200
- Test update logo image URL → expect 200
- Test update all fields → expect 200
- Test update profile without authentication → expect 401
- Test update profile as customer → expect 403

##### **POST /v1/sellers/approve**
- Test admin approves seller → expect 200
- Test admin rejects seller → expect 200 and rejection reason saved
- Test approve non-existing seller → expect 404
- Test approve as non-admin → expect 403
- Test reject with no reason → expect 400

##### **POST /v1/sellers/reapply**
- Test rejected seller re-applies → expect 201
- Test approved seller re-applies → expect 403
- Test suspended seller re-applies → expect 403
- Test reapply without authentication → expect 401

##### **DELETE /v1/sellers/account**
- Test seller account deletion with no pending orders → expect 204
- Test seller account deletion with pending paid order → expect 400
- Test seller account deletion with pending cancellation → expect 400
- Test seller account deletion with pending refund → expect 400
- Test deletion without authentication → expect 401


#### **Category Management API Tests**

##### **GET /v1/categories**
- Test get all categories (with subcategories) → expect 200 with tree structure
- Test get categories with no subcategories → expect 200 with flat structure
- Test get categories as unauthenticated → expect 200

##### **GET /v1/categories/{categoryId}**
- Test get single category → expect 200
- Test get non-existent category → expect 404
- Test get as unauthenticated → expect 200

##### **POST /v1/categories**
- Test admin creates root category → expect 201
- Test admin creates subcategory → expect 201
- Test create category with no name → expect 400
- Test create category as non-admin → expect 403

##### **PUT /v1/categories/{categoryId}**
- Test admin updates category name → expect 200
- Test admin updates category description → expect 200
- Test update non-existent category → expect 404
- Test update category as non-admin → expect 403

##### **DELETE /v1/categories/{categoryId}**
- Test admin deletes category → expect 204
- Test delete root category with subcategories → expect 204 (uncategorized products)
- Test delete non-existent category → expect 404
- Test delete category as non-admin → expect 403


#### **Product Management API Tests**

##### **POST /v1/products**
- Test seller creates product with valid data → expect 201
- Test create product with missing name → expect 400
- Test create product with missing description → expect 400
- Test create product with invalid category → expect 400
- Test create product as customer → expect 403
- Test create product with basePrice < 0 → expect 400

##### **GET /v1/products/{productId}**
- Test get public product details → expect 200 with all fields
- Test get deleted product → expect 404
- Test get product with no variants → expect 200 with isAvailable=false
- Test get non-existent product → expect 404

##### **PUT /v1/products/{productId}**
- Test seller updates product name → expect 200
- Test seller updates description, category, base price → expect 200
- Test update product not owned by user → expect 403
- Test update as customer → expect 403
- Test update non-existent product → expect 404

##### **DELETE /v1/products/{productId}**
- Test seller deletes product with no pending order items → expect 204
- Test delete product with pending paid order item → expect 400
- Test delete product with pending cancellation → expect 400
- Test delete non-existent product → expect 404
- Test delete as customer → expect 403

##### **GET /v1/products/{productId}/snapshots**
- Test seller retrieves product snapshots → expect 200
- Test admin retrieves product snapshots → expect 200
- Test customer retrieves product snapshots → expect 403
- Test get snapshots for non-existent product → expect 404


#### **Product Image Management API Tests**

##### **POST /v1/products/{productId}/images**
- Test seller uploads image → expect 201
- Test upload image to non-existent product → expect 404
- Test upload image as customer → expect 403
- Test upload invalid file type → expect 400

##### **PUT /v1/products/{productId}/images/reorder**
- Test reorder images → expect 200 with updated order
- Test reorder with invalid imageId → expect 400
- Test reorder as non-seller → expect 403
- Test reorder non-existent product → expect 404

##### **DELETE /v1/products/{productId}/images/{imageId}**
- Test delete image → expect 204
- Test delete non-existent image → expect 404
- Test delete image from product not owned → expect 403
- Test delete main image → expect 204


#### **Product Variant (SKU) Management API Tests**

##### **POST /v1/products/{productId}/variants**
- Test seller creates variant with valid SKU → expect 201
- Test create variant with duplicated SKU → expect 409
- Test create variant with invalid options format → expect 400
- Test create variant with stock < 0 → expect 400
- Test create variant as customer → expect 403

##### **PUT /v1/products/{productId}/variants/{variantId}**
- Test seller updates variant price → expect 200
- Test seller updates variant stock → expect 200
- Test update variant with invalid SKU → expect 409
- Test update variant as customer → expect 403
- Test update non-existent variant → expect 404

##### **DELETE /v1/products/{productId}/variants/{variantId}**
- Test seller deletes variant with no pending orders → expect 204
- Test delete variant with paid order item → expect 400
- Test delete non-existent variant → expect 404
- Test delete as customer → expect 403

##### **GET /v1/products/{productId}/variants**
- Test get all variants → expect 200
- Test get variants for non-existent product → expect 404
- Test get variants as unauthenticated → expect 200


#### **Inventory Management API Tests**

##### **POST /v1/inventory/add**
- Test seller adds inventory → expect 201
- Test add negative quantity → expect 400
- Test add to non-existent variant → expect 404
- Test add as customer → expect 403

##### **POST /v1/inventory/subtract**
- Test seller subtracts inventory → expect 201
- Test subtract negative quantity → expect 400
- Test subtract from non-existent variant → expect 404
- Test subtract as customer → expect 403

##### **GET /v1/inventory/{variantId}/history**
- Test get inventory history → expect 200
- Test get history for non-existent variant → expect 404
- Test get history as customer → expect 403


#### **Wishlist API Tests**

##### **GET /v1/wishlist**
- Test get customer wishlist → expect 200 with items
- Test get empty wishlist → expect 200 with empty array
- Test get wishlist as seller → expect 403
- Test get wishlist without auth → expect 401

##### **POST /v1/wishlist**
- Test add product to wishlist → expect 201
- Test add non-existent product → expect 404
- Test add already-owned product → expect 409
- Test add as seller → expect 403
- Test add without auth → expect 401

##### **DELETE /v1/wishlist/{productId}**
- Test remove product from wishlist → expect 204

import { ArrayUtil, RandomGenerator } from "@nestia/e2e";
import { randint } from "tstl";
import typia, { tags } from "typia";

import { DeepPartial } from "@ORGANIZATION/PROJECT-api/lib/typings/DeepPartial";
import { IEntity } from "@ORGANIZATION/PROJECT-api/lib/structures/IEntity";
import { IShoppingMallConfiguration } from "@ORGANIZATION/PROJECT-api/lib/structures/IShoppingMallConfiguration";
export function prepare_random_shopping_mall_configuration(
  input?: DeepPartial<IShoppingMallConfiguration.ICreate>,
): IShoppingMallConfiguration.ICreate {
  return {
    currency:
      input?.currency ??
      RandomGenerator.pick(["USD", "EUR", "JPY", "KRW", "GBP"] as const),
    payment:
      input?.payment ??
      RandomGenerator.pick([
        "stripe",
        "paypal",
        "square",
        "razorpay",
        "klarna",
      ] as const),
    tax:
      input?.tax ??
      typia.random<
        number & tags.Type<"float"> & tags.Minimum<0> & tags.Maximum<0.3>
      >(),
    email: input?.email ?? typia.random<string & tags.Format<"email">>(),
    category:
      input?.category ??
      RandomGenerator.pick([
        "electronics",
        "books",
        "clothing",
        "home",
        "sports",
      ] as const),
    timezone:
      input?.timezone ??
      RandomGenerator.pick([
        "Asia/Seoul",
        "Asia/Tokyo",
        "America/New_York",
        "Europe/London",
        "Australia/Sydney",
      ] as const),
    currency_exchange_rate_source:
      input?.currency_exchange_rate_source ??
      RandomGenerator.pick([
        "openexchangerates",
        "fixer",
        "central_bank",
        "manual",
      ] as const),
    default_language:
      input?.default_language ??
      RandomGenerator.pick([
        "en-US",
        "ko-KR",
        "ja-JP",
        "zh-CN",
        "es-ES",
      ] as const),
    api_rate_limit:
      input?.api_rate_limit ??
      typia.random<
        number & tags.Type<"uint32"> & tags.Minimum<10> & tags.Maximum<100>
      >(),
    checkout_timeout_minutes:
      input?.checkout_timeout_minutes ??
      typia.random<
        number & tags.Type<"uint32"> & tags.Minimum<5> & tags.Maximum<30>
      >(),
    enable_guest_checkout:
      input?.enable_guest_checkout ??
      RandomGenerator.pick([true, false] as const),
    min_order_value_for_free_shipping:
      input?.min_order_value_for_free_shipping ??
      typia.random<
        number & tags.Type<"uint32"> & tags.Minimum<1000> & tags.Maximum<10000>
      >(),
    max_shipping_days:
      input?.max_shipping_days ??
      typia.random<
        number & tags.Type<"uint32"> & tags.Minimum<1> & tags.Maximum<15>
      >(),
    return_period_days:
      input?.return_period_days ??
      typia.random<
        number & tags.Type<"uint32"> & tags.Minimum<14> & tags.Maximum<60>
      >(),
    tax_inclusive_pricing:
      input?.tax_inclusive_pricing ??
      RandomGenerator.pick([true, false] as const),
    product_search_enabled:
      input?.product_search_enabled ??
      RandomGenerator.pick([true, false] as const),
    enable_catalog_search:
      input?.enable_catalog_search ??
      RandomGenerator.pick([true, false] as const),
    inventory_reservation_enabled:
      input?.inventory_reservation_enabled ??
      RandomGenerator.pick([true, false] as const),
    shipping_tax_calculation:
      input?.shipping_tax_calculation ??
      RandomGenerator.pick(["included", "separate", "automatic"] as const),
    customer_service_phone:
      input?.customer_service_phone ?? RandomGenerator.mobile("+82"),
    order_number_prefix:
      input?.order_number_prefix ??
      RandomGenerator.pick(["ORD", "SHOP", "INV", "SL"] as const),
    gift_card_enabled:
      input?.gift_card_enabled ?? RandomGenerator.pick([true, false] as const),
    affiliate_program_enabled:
      input?.affiliate_program_enabled ??
      RandomGenerator.pick([true, false] as const),
    referral_program_enabled:
      input?.referral_program_enabled ??
      RandomGenerator.pick([true, false] as const),
    newsletter_subscription_enabled:
      input?.newsletter_subscription_enabled ??
      RandomGenerator.pick([true, false] as const),
    marketing_emails_enabled:
      input?.marketing_emails_enabled ??
      RandomGenerator.pick([true, false] as const),
    default_shipping_method:
      input?.default_shipping_method ??
      RandomGenerator.pick([
        "standard",
        "express",
        "overnight",
        "pickup",
      ] as const),
    max_items_per_cart:
      input?.max_items_per_cart ??
      typia.random<
        number & tags.Type<"uint32"> & tags.Minimum<20> & tags.Maximum<100>
      >(),
    order_confirmation_template:
      input?.order_confirmation_template ??
      RandomGenerator.pick([
        "standard",
        "premium",
        "simple",
        "extended",
      ] as const),
    return_policy_url:
      input?.return_policy_url ?? typia.random<string & tags.Format<"url">>(),
    payment_method_display_order:
      input?.payment_method_display_order ??
      RandomGenerator.pick([
        "stripe,paypal,credit_card",
        "paypal,stripe,credit_card",
        "credit_card,stripe,paypal",
      ] as const),
    minimum_password_length:
      input?.minimum_password_length ??
      typia.random<
        number & tags.Type<"uint32"> & tags.Minimum<8> & tags.Maximum<20>
      >(),
    captcha_enabled:
      input?.captcha_enabled ?? RandomGenerator.pick([true, false] as const),
    enable_email_notifications:
      input?.enable_email_notifications ??
      RandomGenerator.pick([true, false] as const),
    enable_sms_notifications:
      input?.enable_sms_notifications ??
      RandomGenerator.pick([true, false] as const),
    notification_email:
      input?.notification_email ??
      typia.random<string & tags.Format<"email">>(),
    support_email:
      input?.support_email ?? typia.random<string & tags.Format<"email">>(),
    default_category_id:
      input?.default_category_id ??
      typia.random<string & tags.Format<"uuid">>(),
    max_product_images:
      input?.max_product_images ??
      typia.random<
        number & tags.Type<"uint32"> & tags.Minimum<3> & tags.Maximum<10>
      >(),
    allowed_file_extensions:
      input?.allowed_file_extensions ??
      RandomGenerator.pick([
        "jpg,jpeg,png,gif,pdf",
        "webp,jpg,png,jpeg",
        "png,jpeg",
      ] as const),
  };
}

instruction:
### Implementation Instructions for Realize Agent

#### **Authentication Service Implementation**

##### **Auth Service Logic**
- Implement user registration: create user record with hashed password (bcrypt), set role (customer/seller)
- Implement login: verify password hash, issue JWT with 15min expiry and refresh token with 7d expiry
- Implement password change: validate current password, update password_hash, invalidate all sessions
- Implement account deletion: set is_active=false, deleted_at=now; preserve orders and reviews
- Implement token refresh: validate refresh token, issue new access token, rotate refresh token
- Implement rate limiting on auth endpoints (5 attempts/min)

##### **Auth Middleware**
- Create JWT authentication guard that decodes token and attaches user to request
- Implement role guard (CustomerGuard, SellerGuard, AdminGuard, SuperAdminGuard)
- Implement ban check middleware: reject requests if user.is_banned=true
- Implement inactive account check middleware: reject requests if user.is_active=false

#### **Customer Profile Service**

##### **Customer Profile Logic**
- Implement profile retrieval: return customer.display_name, phone_number
- Implement profile update: update display_name, phone_number, set updated_at=now
- Include validation: phone_number must be valid E.164 format
- Include audit: log updates via Prisma but do not create snapshot (profile changes are not snapshotted per requirements)

#### **Address Service**

##### **Address Service Logic**
- Implement address creation: validate required fields, ensure user owns account
- Implement address update: validate user ownership, update fields
- Implement address deletion: soft delete using is_deleted flag
- Implement default address setting:
  - When setting is_default=true for any address, set is_default=false for all other addresses by same customer
  - When deleting default address, auto-set another as default (if exists) or null
- Implement address list retrieval: filter by customer_id, exclude deleted addresses
- Implement default address retrieval: find the active default address for user

#### **Seller Account Service**

##### **Seller Account Logic**
- Implement seller registration: create user with role=seller, is_approved=false
- Implement seller approval/rejection:
  - On approve: set is_approved=true, approval_rejection_reason=null
  - On reject: set is_approved=false, approval_rejection_reason=requested_reason
- Implement seller reapplication: allow rejected sellers to submit new registration (reset is_approved=false, approval_rejection_reason=null)
- Implement seller deletion validation:
  - Check for pending order items (status=paid OR shipped)
  - Check for pending cancellation requests (status=pending)
  - Check for pending refund requests (status=pending)
  - If any present, throw error; else, soft delete (set is_active=false)
- Implement seller suspension:
  - On suspend: set is_suspended=true, suspension_reason=requested_reason, hide products
  - On unsuspend: set is_suspended=false, suspension_reason=null, unhide products
- Implement seller profile retrieval: return shop_name, shop_description, logo_image_url, approval_status, is_suspended
- Implement seller profile update:
  - Update shop_name, shop_description, logo_image_url
  - Trigger snapshot creation (see snapshot logic below)

#### **Category Service**

##### **Category Logic**
- Implement category tree retrieval: use recursive query to fetch categories with nested children
- Implement category creation (admin-only): ensure parent_category_id is valid category, name is unique
- Implement category update (admin-only): update name/description, validate uniqueness
- Implement category deletion (admin-only): 
  - Set all products in category to category_id=null (uncategorized)
  - Set parent_category_id=null for all subcategories
  - Soft delete category (is_deleted=true)

#### **Product Service**

##### **Product Logic**
- Implement product creation (seller-only):
  - Create product record
  - Set seller_id=authenticated seller
  - Validate category exists and is not deleted
- Implement product update (seller-only):
  - Validate product belongs to seller
  - Update name, description, category_id, base_price
  - Trigger product snapshot creation (see snapshot logic below)
- Implement product deletion:
  - Validate product belongs to seller
  - Validate no pending order items (status=paid OR shipped) for any variant
  - Validate no pending cancellation/refund requests for any variant
  - If valid: set is_deleted=true, deleted_at=now
- Implement product retrieval:
  - Public: return non-deleted products with variant count and average rating
  - For seller/admin: include deleted products
- Implement product snapshot creation:
  - Create product_snapshot record with current product state
  - Create product_snapshot_sku records for all active variants
  - Store images as JSONB array with image_url and image_order
  - Trigger on: product creation, product update

#### **Product Image Service**

##### **Product Image Logic**
- Implement image upload:
  - Generate unique UUID filename
  - Store in cloud storage (S3/Cloudinary) - assume integration exists
  - Save record with product_id, image_url, image_order=(current_max_order+1)
- Implement image reorder:
  - Validate all imageIds belong to product
  - Update image_order for each image based on input
  - Trigger product snapshot creation
- Implement image deletion:
  - Validate image belongs to product
  - Delete from cloud storage
  - Soft delete in DB (is_deleted=true)
  - Trigger product snapshot creation

#### **Product Variant (SKU) Service**

##### **Product Variant Logic**
- Implement variant creation (seller-only):
  - Validate product exists and belongs to seller
  - Validate SKU code is unique per product
  - Validate option_values is valid JSONB object
  - Create variant record with stock_quantity=0
  - Validate product has at least one variant after creation
- Implement variant update (seller-only):
  - Validate variant belongs to seller's product
  - Update sku_code, option_values, price, stock_quantity
  - Validate sku_code remains unique per product
  - Trigger product variant snapshot creation (see below)
- Implement variant deletion:
  - Validate variant belongs to seller's product
  - Validate no pending order items (status=paid OR shipped)
  - Validate no pending cancellation/refund requests
  - If valid: set is_deleted=true, deleted_at=now
- Implement variant retrieval:
  - Public: return active variants (is_deleted=false)
  - For seller/admin: return all variants
  - Calculate availability: product is available if at least one variant is active and non-deleted
- Implement variant snapshot creation (on update):
  - Create product_snapshot_sku record with current state
  - Include sku_code, option_values, price, stock_quantity

#### **Inventory Service**

##### **Inventory Logic**
- Implement inventory addition (restock):
  - Create inventory record with positive quantity_change
  - Reason: provided by seller
  - Source_type: restock
- Implement inventory subtraction (adjustment):
  - Create inventory record with negative quantity_change
  - Reason: provided by seller
  - Source_type: adjustment
- Implement inventory calculation:
  - For any variant: SUM(quantity_change) FROM inventory_record WHERE variant_id=??? AND created_at<=now()
- Implement inventory history retrieval (seller-only):
  - Return all records for variant, ordered by created_at DESC
  - Include source_id for reverse lookup

#### **Wishlist Service**

##### **Wishlist Logic**
- Implement add to wishlist:
  - Validate product exists and not deleted
  - Create wishlist entry with customer_id, product_id
  - Prevent duplicates (upsert if duplicate exists)
- Implement remove from wishlist:
  - Delete wishlist entry
- Implement get wishlist:
  - Join with product to get product name, seller_name, main_image_url
  - Exclude deleted products
- Implement cleanup on product deletion:
  - On product deletion (soft delete), trigger deletion of all wishlist entries for that product

#### **Shopping Cart Service**

##### **Shopping Cart Logic**
- Implement add to cart:
  - Validate variant exists and is_active and not deleted
  - If cart item already exists for variant: increment quantity
  - Else: create new cart item
  - Add warning if stock_quantity < new_quantity
- Implement update cart quantity:
  - Validate variant exists and is_active and not deleted
  - If quantity=0: delete cart item
  - Else: update quantity
  - Add warning if stock_quantity < new_quantity
- Implement remove from cart:
  - Delete cart item
- Implement clear cart:
  - Delete all cart items for customer
- Implement get cart:
  - Join with variant, product, seller to get full details
  - Add is_available flag: variant.is_deleted=false AND stock_quantity>0
  - Include warning if stock_quantity < cart_quantity
  - Calculate subtotal = quantity * price_at_cart_time
  - Calculate total = sum(subtotal)
- Implement cart validation before checkout:
  - Check that all cart items are available (is_available=true)
  - Reject checkout if any item is unavailable

#### **Checkout Service**

##### **Checkout Logic**
- Implement checkout initiation:
  - Validate cart is not empty
  - Validate cart items are all available
  - Validate shipping address belongs to user
  - Create order record with status=pending
  - Calculate total_price = sum(cart_items.quantity * variant_price)
  - Create order_items for each cart item:
    - status=paid
    - quantity=cart_quantity
    - price_at_time=variant_price
    - product_id, variant_id, seller_id
  - Clear cart
- Implement checkout completion:
  - Validate payment gateway response
  - If successful:
    - Set order.payment_status=succeeded
    - Trigger inventory deduction:
      - For each order_item: create inventory_record with negative quantity_change, source_type=order_placement, source_id=order_id
    - Create order_item snapshots:
      - product_snapshot_id, product_snapshot_sku_id, seller_profile_snapshot_id from latest snapshots at time of checkout
  - If payment fails:
    - Set order.payment_status=failed
    - Revert inventory calculations (do not create inventory records)
    - Return cart items to cart (recreate cart items with same quantities)
- Implement payment integration:
  - No payment logic needed - assume external gateway provides webhook confirmation

#### **Order Service**

##### **Order Logic**
- Implement order retrieval:
  - Customer: only own orders
  - Admin: all orders
  - Return order status derived from items:
    - all paid → "paid"
    - any shipped + no delivered → "shipped"
    - all delivered → "delivered"
    - all cancelled → "cancelled"
    - all refunded → "refunded"
    - mixed → "partially_completed"
- Implement order detail retrieval:
  - Include order_items with:
    - product_snapshot, variant_snapshot, seller_profile_snapshot
  - Include shipments (grouped by seller_id)

#### **Shipping and Tracking Service**

##### **Shipping Logic**
- Implement get pending items (seller view):
  - Filter order_items by seller_id AND status=paid
- Implement create shipment:
  - Validate all order_items belong to same seller
  - Validate all items have status=paid
  - Create shipment record with carrier_name, tracking_number
  - Update all included order_items to status=shipped
- Implement deliver shipment:
  - On admin/automated: if shipment.created_at + 14 days < now() AND is_delivered=false, set is_delivered=true, delivered_at=now()
  - On customer confirmation: set is_delivered=true, delivered_at=now()
  - Update all order_items in shipment to status=delivered

#### **Order Cancellation Service**

##### **Cancellation Logic**
- Implement cancellation request:
  - Validate order_item.status=paid
  - Validate order_item belongs to user
  - Create cancellation_request record with reason, status=pending, requested_at=now()
- Implement cancellation response:
  - Validate seller owns product
  - Update cancellation_request:
    - status=approved/rejected
    - responded_at=now()
    - responded_by=authenticated admin/seller id
  - Create cancellation_request_snapshot
  - On approval:
    - Set order_item.status=cancelled
    - Create positive inventory_record (source_type=order_cancellation)
- Implement status derivation:
  - If all order_items in order are cancelled → set order.status=cancelled

#### **Refund Service**

##### **Refund Logic**
- Implement refund request:
  - Validate order_item.status=delivered
  - Validate current_time <= order_item.updated_at + 7 days
  - Validate order_item belongs to user
  - Create refund_request record with reason, status=pending, requested_at=now()
- Implement refund response:
  - Validate seller owns product
  - Update refund_request:
    - status=approved/rejected
    - responded_at=now()
    - responded_by=authenticated admin/seller id
  - Create refund_request_snapshot
  - On approval:
    - Set order_item.status=refunded
    - Create positive inventory_record (source_type=order_refund)
- Implement status derivation:
  - If all order_items in order are refunded → set order.status=refunded

#### **Review Service**

##### **Review Logic**
- Implement review creation:
  - Validate order_item.status=delivered
  - Validate user hasn't reviewed this product per order before (unique constraint: customer_id + product_id + order_id)
  - Create review record with rating, text
- Implement review update:
  - Validate review belongs to user
  - Update rating, text
  - Trigger review_snapshot creation
- Implement review deletion:
  - Validate review belongs to user
  - Set is_deleted=true, deleted_at=now
  - Preserve snapshot
- Implement review retrieval:
  - Return all reviews for product where is_deleted=false
  - Calculate average_rating = AVG(rating) FROM reviews WHERE product_id=???
  - Count total non-deleted reviews
- Implement review snapshot creation:
  - On update/delete: create snapshot with current state

#### **Seller Dashboard Service**

##### **Dashboard Logic**
- Implement dashboard summary:
  - Total products: COUNT(products WHERE seller_id=???)
  - Total order items: COUNT(order_items WHERE seller_id=???)
  - Pending cancellations: COUNT(cancellation_requests WHERE status=pending AND order_item.seller_id=???)
  - Pending refunds: COUNT(refund_requests WHERE status=pending AND order_item.seller_id=???)
- Implement order items listing:
  - Filter by seller_id
  - Apply status filter if provided
  - Return with customer info

#### **Administrator Service**

##### **Admin Request Logic**
- Implement administrator application:
  - Validate user exists and has role=customer or seller
  - Create admin_request record with reason, status=pending
- Implement admin request review (super admin only):
  - On approve:
    - Set user.role=admin, user.admin_type=regular
    - Set admin_request.status=approved, responded_at=now()
  - On reject:
    - Set admin_request.status=rejected, responded_at=now(), rejected_reason=reason
- Implement admin promotion:
  - Validate target admin exists and is not super
  - Validate caller is a super admin
  - Update admin_type=super
- Implement admin demotion:
  - Validate target admin exists and is super
  - Validate caller is a super admin
  - Validate target is not the same as caller
  - Update admin_type=regular

##### **Seller Management Logic**
- Implement seller approval:
  - Set seller.is_approved=true
  - Set seller.approval_rejection_reason=null
- Implement seller rejection:
  - Set seller.is_approved=false
  - Set seller.approval_rejection_reason=reason
- Implement seller suspension:
  - Set seller.is_suspended=true
  - Set seller.suspension_reason=reason
  - Set all seller.products.is_hidden=true
- Implement seller unsuspension:
  - Set seller.is_suspended=false
  - Set seller.suspension_reason=null
  - Set all seller.products.is_hidden=false
- Implement seller ban:
  - Set seller.is_banned=true
- Implement seller unban:
  - Set seller.is_banned=false

##### **Product Oversight Logic**
- Implement admin product deletion:
  - Set product.is_deleted=true, deleted_at=now()
  - Set all variants.is_deleted=true, deleted_at=now()
  - Delete all inventory records
  - Do NOT trigger product snapshot (since admin deletion bypasses normal snapshot rules)
  - Notify seller

##### **Order Oversight Logic**
- Implement admin force-cancel:
  - Set order_item.status=cancelled
  - Create positive inventory_record (source_type=admin_cancel)
  - Create cancellation_request snapshot
- Implement admin force-refund:
  - Set order_item.status=refunded
  - Create positive inventory_record (source_type=admin_refund)
  - Create refund_request snapshot

##### **User Management Logic**
- Implement customer ban:
  - Set customer.is_banned=true
- Implement customer unban:
  - Set customer.is_banned=false

#### **Snapshot Service**

##### **Snapshot Logic**
- General snapshot pattern:
  - Every time any tracked entity is updated or deleted:
    1. Retrieve current state
    2. Create snapshot record:
       - snapshot_id
       - entity_type: product | product_variant | seller_profile | order_item | review | cancellation_request | refund_request
       - entity_id
       - version: 1 if create, 2+ if update
       - created_at: current UTC datetime
       - action: create | update | delete
       - previous_values: JSONB of entity state before change
       - current_values: JSONB of entity state after change
       - created_by: user_id
    3. For product snapshots: create product_snapshot record
    4. For product variant snapshots: create product_snapshot_sku record
    5. For seller profile snapshots: create seller_profile_snapshot record
    6. For order item snapshots: create order_item_snapshot record
    7. For review snapshots: create review_snapshot record
    8. For cancellation request snapshots: create cancellation_request_snapshot record
    9. For refund request snapshots: create refund_request_snapshot record
- Implement snapshot retrieval:
  - Seller/admin can view snapshots
  - Filter by owner/user when applicable
- Implement snapshot immutability:
  - All snapshot records are READ-ONLY
  - No UPDATE/DELETE allowed on snapshot tables

#### **Search Service**

##### **Search Logic**
- Implement product search:
  - Full-text search on product name
  - Filter by category: join with category hierarchy
  - Filter by price range: compare base_price or variant min/max
  - Filter by inStockOnly: check if ANY variant has stock > 0
  - Sort by newest: order by product.created_at DESC
  - Sort by price_asc: order by variant.min_price ASC
  - Sort by price_desc: order by variant.max_price DESC
  - Pagination: use SKIP/LIMIT
  - Include: product.id, name, base_price, category_name, seller_name, main_image_url, avg_rating, review_count, is_available

#### **Event Listeners**

- Implement triggers for:
  - After product update → create product snapshot
  - After variant update → create product variant snapshot
  - After seller profile update → create seller profile snapshot
  - After order creation → create order item snapshots
  - After review update → create review snapshot
  - After cancellation/refund request update → create request snapshot
  - After product deletion → auto-remove from wishlist

#### **Validation Rules**

- Implement field validation:
  - email: email regex pattern
  - password: min 8, must contain letter and number
  - phone_number: E.164 format
  - price: >= 0
  - stock_quantity: >= 0
  - rating: 1-5
  - quantity: > 0
  - SKU code: unique per product
- Implement ownership validation:
  - All write operations on user data must validate user_id matches
  - All product operations must validate seller_id matches
- Implement business rule validations:
  - Cannot delete seller with pending orders
  - Cannot delete product with pending order items
  - Cannot delete variant with pending order items
  - Cannot cancel item after shipped
  - Cannot refund item after 7 days or before delivered
  - Cannot have more than 1 default address
  - Cannot have product with no variants
- Implement concurrent update protection:
  - Use optimistic locking on inventory and stock quantities
  - Use Prisma's native versioning where possible
  - Use transactions for multi-table operations (checkout, inventory change)

#### **Database Schema Implementation**

- Use Prisma ORM with PostgreSQL
- Define all tables as per database specification
- Use UUID as primary key type
- Use JSONB for dynamic fields
- Use ENUM types for status fields
- Use soft deletes (is_deleted, deleted_at)
- Use timestamp with timezone

#### **Security Implementation**

- Hash passwords with bcrypt
- Use JWT with HS256 for authentication
- Validate JWT signature and expiry
- Implement role-based access control (RBAC) for all endpoints
- Sanitize all inputs
- Prevent SQL injection
- Protect against XSS
- Validate file types on image uploads
- Use rate limiting
- Use HTTPS

#### **Performance Optimization**

- Indexes:
  - user(email)
  - product(seller_id, is_deleted)
  - product_variant(sku_code)
  - inventory_record(variant_id, created_at)
  - review(customer_id, product_id)
  - order(customer_id, created_at)
  - order_item(order_id, status)
  - shipment(order_id, seller_id)
  - wishlist(customer_id, product_id)
  - cart(customer_id, variant_id)
  - snapshot(entity_type, entity_id, version)
- Use proper eager loading (Prisma include)
- Cache product listings and search results (Redis recommended)
- Use database query optimization (avoid N+1)
- Limit returned fields where possible

#### **Error Handling**

- Use structured error responses
- Include HTTP status, error code, message
- Log all errors
- Never expose internal stack traces
- Validate all inputs before processing

#### **Testing Coverage**

- All business logic tests must pass
- All endpoint E2E tests must pass
- Snapshot creation must be verified for all tracked entities
- Inventory calculation must match sum of records

#### **Deployment**

- Use NestJS with TypeScript
- Use Prisma as ORM
- Use PostgreSQL as database
- Use JWT for authentication
- Use environment variables for secrets
- Containerize with Docker
- Use CI/CD pipeline

#### **Future-Proofing**

- Design to support: multi-currency, region-based pricing
- Use UTC timestamps consistently
- Use UUID consistently
- Use OpenAPI/Swagger for API documentation
- Include proper logging
- Maintain backward compatibility
- Use versioned API endpoints (/v1/)
